A second thing it must wait for cannot be written down at all: the list it lives on cannot refer to an item on the other list, so that one is recorded in words at the top of its notes and has been given its own item to fix.

notes only, no dependency changed, and no second item authored because one already exists. The item gains that evidence, the constraint it implies for how the fix must be built, and a correction to two stale line references.

authored. Six finished pieces of database work have been built and approved and never switched on in the live system, and no item on either list turns them on. escalations.title: The credential lockdown, the one action that closes off every temporary permission the overnight sessions hold, is waiting on the extraction supplier and has been since 2026-08-27. As long as he does not answer, permissions that were granted as temporary stay live.
escalations.recommendation: Set a date and do the lockdown on it, rather than waiting for him. RECOMMENDED BECAUSE THE ONLY THING HIS ANSWER BUYS IS ONE TEST: the item waiting on him is a single live document run through the supplier's system, and it is the only thing that genuinely needs the current credentials in place. Everything else the lockdown removes has nothing to do with him. THE HONEST TRADEOFF, STATED SO YOU ARE NOT SURPRISED: doing the lockdown first means that live document run needs fresh credentials afterwards, which is half an hour of setup, not a rebuild. Waiting means the temporary permissions stay live indefinitely on somebody else's schedule. There is a third option if you prefer: chase him for a date, and if he does not give one within a week, the lockdown goes ahead anyway. IF UNANSWERED: nothing breaks and nothing gets worse, which is precisely the problem. The permissions stay live, the lockdown stays unscheduled, and the client acceptance walk stays behind it, exactly as it has for eight days.

escalations.title: Two settings in the live hosting environment for the low-stock warning email have been recorded inside a readiness condition since 2026-08-26 and are still not confirmed set. This is the third time it has been raised.
escalations.recommendation: Set RESEND_API_KEY and RESEND_FROM in the PRODUCTION environment, by name only, and reply that they are set. RECOMMENDED BECAUSE THEY COST NOTHING AND ARE ON THE CRITICAL PATH ANYWAY: both are already required items on the credential lockdown checklist, so doing them now removes two items from that day rather than adding any. THE HONEST CAVEAT, REPEATED BECAUSE IT IS THE PART THAT GETS LOST: this does NOT make the condition pass. The warning email is currently addressed to an account on a domain that does not exist, so even with both settings in place it would be sent to nobody. That third piece lands with the real staff accounts at the lockdown. IF UNANSWERED: nothing breaks. The warning email keeps recording its reason on screen and not sending, which is the designed behaviour, and both settings simply wait to be done on lockdown day instead.
